notes: trome.com: robots.txt HTTP 200, permissive (User-agent: * Disallow:) and advertises https://trome.com/sitemap/?outputType=xml. That is a sitemapindex of 10 per-section sitemaps (celebrities, horoscopo, viral, mundo, usa, actualidad, deportes, familia, emprende-trome, impresa); all 10 fetched HTTP 200 (11s total, 11 requests). Each is a flat urlset of <loc>+<lastmod>, newest first. Five files are capped at exactly 1000 entries, but each reaches back well past the window start (actualidad oldest 2026-09-03, deportes 2026-06-13, familia 2025-11-23, horoscopo 2024-02, impresa 2024-01), so the window 2026-09-25..2026-10-25 is fully covered by the 10 files; the 'usa' (max 2026-08-27) and 'viral' (max 2026-09-28) sections are simply stale. 5610 entries, 5521 unique URLs; 89 URLs appear in two section sitemaps (kept the earlier lastmod on conflict). Date source: <lastmod> in site-local time (America/Lima -05:00, no DST). I verified lastmod is the PUBLICATION time, not edit time: 10 random in-window articles sampled across 09-25/09-30/10-10/10-20/10-25 had sitemap lastmod equal to page JSON-LD datePublished to the millisecond (e.g. lastmod 2026-09-25T21:39-05:00 == datePublished 2026-09-26T02:39:00Z; -05:00 converts to +1 day in UTC, which the 1-day check tolerance covers). The script re-runs that spot check with a fixed seed (25 URLs) at runtime and printed 0 mismatches. Filtered to window -> 916 unique URLs, all 31 days present, min day 21 (2026-09-26), target days 2026-09-30=27, 2026-10-10=23, 2026-10-20=43 (all >=15). I then simulated the judge: 4 random samples all HTTP 200 with 5950-8828 stripped chars of text and page date exactly equal to the listed date (diff=0). Runtime 23s wall. Final route works because it is 2 levels of the site's own XML with per-entry publication timestamps; no archive pages, RSS or Wayback needed.
